## Before submitting

- [ ] I agree to license this contribution under the terms of [LICENSE.txt](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/LICENSE.txt).
- [x] I ran `pre-commit run` and committed any formatting changes.
- [x] I reviewed the Hard Rules in the `AGENTS.md` for each directory this PR touches (see [root AGENTS.md § Reviewing a PR](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/AGENTS.md#reviewing-a-pr-human-or-agent)) and my changes comply, or I explain the exception below.
- [x] I added GitHub labels: one `cat-*`, one or more `area:*` / `op:*`, and one `orig-*` (see [label list](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/labels)).

## Affected area

CI or test infrastructure

## Summary

`gated_attention_block_qsa_reference` computes its projection as one fp32 GEMM over all 1408 columns of `w_qkvg`: 768 dense columns plus the 640-column INDEX band. `test_the_index_band_is_split_off_and_exposed` compares that output against the dense oracle, which runs the same GEMM at N = 768, with a 1e-5 bound documented as "bitwise in practice".

On some GPUs cuBLAS reduces the shared columns in a different order at the two N. This PR makes the QSA oracle run the dense columns and the band as two GEMMs. Each output element is still one fp32 dot product rounded once, so the oracle's math is unchanged; only the reduction order becomes independent of the band. A stale comment in the test is updated in place.

## Why

Fixed inputs (`seed=15`, `h` [1, 64, 256]), fp32 with TF32 off. The table counts how many of the 768 shared columns differ between the N = 1408 and N = 768 GEMMs:

| GPU | fp32 values differing (of 49152) | after bf16 rounding | test before |
|---|---|---|---|
| L40S | 30617 | 6 | **fails**: `out: max rel diff 6.868e-04 > 1e-05` |
| A100 | 28130 | 7 | passes |
| H100 | 0 | 0 | passes |
| B200 | 0 | 0 | passes |

A100 also has differing values but stays under the 1e-5 bound. CI runs this test on sm80/90/100/107 but has no sm89 cutedsl lane, so the L40S failure only shows up locally.

## Related issues

Related to #1639, which added the oracle and the test.

## API and compatibility impact

None. Test oracle only.

## Testing

- **The failing test on all four GPUs**, after this change: `pytest gated_attention_block/cutedsl/test_gated_block_qsa_reference.py -k test_the_index_band_is_split_off_and_exposed` passes on L40S, A100, H100 and B200. The band now matches the indexer's `k_raw` bitwise: 8192/8192, max diff 0.
- **The full set of QSA test files that import this oracle** (`test_gated_block_qsa_reference`, `_vs_transformers`, `test_block_qsa*`):
  - L40S: 132 passed, 105 skipped.
  - B200: 131 passed, 1 failed, 105 skipped. The failure is `TestIdentityBound::test_adversarial_plant_makes_the_dropped_block_matter` (`6.47 > 8.0` nats). It fails identically with the unmodified develop oracle on this host and passes on CI sm100, so this PR does not cause it.
- **Not run locally:** the sm107-only kernel tests.
- **Probe:** `evidence/qsa-index-band-l40s/probe.py` in the workspace.
- **pre-commit:** clean.

detail.title: [Auto-FE] test(gated_attention_block): the QSA oracle's dense columns are the dense oracle's GEMM bitwise on every GPU

files.patch:
@@ -617,7 +617,10 @@ def gated_attention_block_qsa_reference(
     rep = geom.h_q // geom.h_kv
 
     # (1) fused QKV+GATE(+INDEX) projection, fp32 accumulate, one rounding.
-    proj = (h.to(acc_dtype) @ w_qkvg.to(acc_dtype).t()).to(out_dtype)
+    # Dense columns and the band are separate GEMMs: cuBLAS may reduce in a different order at another N (A100 / L40S do),
+    # and the dense columns must match the dense oracle's N = n_dense GEMM bitwise.
+    h_acc = h.to(acc_dtype)
+    proj = torch.cat([h_acc @ w_qkvg[:n_dense].to(acc_dtype).t(), h_acc @ w_qkvg[n_dense:].to(acc_dtype).t()], dim=-1).to(out_dtype)
     q_pre, gate, k_pre, v, band = split_qkvg_qsa(proj, geom, spec)
     index_q_raw = index_k_raw = None
     if band is not None:

@@ -503,7 +503,7 @@ def test_the_index_band_is_split_off_and_exposed(self):
         _assert_oracles_equal(qsa, dense)  # S = 64 < 2051: the band changes nothing of out / O / LSE
         assert qsa.index_k_raw.shape == (1, 64, 128) and qsa.index_q_raw.shape == (1, 64, 4, 128)
         # the band is the slab's last 640 columns, raw: the indexer's own k_raw (pre-norm, un-rotated) within one bf16
-        # rounding -- the same linear map, but a 1408-column GEMM and a 640-column one accumulate in a different order
+        # rounding -- the same linear map; the oracle now runs the band as its own 640-column GEMM, so bitwise in practice
         _s, _ids, _lens, k_raw, _kc = _indexer(inp, g, g.qsa)
         torch.testing.assert_close(qsa.index_k_raw.float(), k_raw.float(), rtol=2**-7, atol=1e-3)
         n_bitwise = int((qsa.index_k_raw == k_raw).sum())
